'''Christine Sutton''' is a particle physicist who edited the ''[[CERN Courier]]'' from 2003 to 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/so-farewell-then/|title = So, farewell then|date = 25 September 2015}}</ref> She retired from CERN in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Our Team|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/our-team|website=cerncourier.com}}</ref>

Sutton was previously based at the [[University of Oxford]], working in the Particle Physics Group and tutoring physics at [[St Catherine's College, Oxford|St Catherine's College]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/Documents/PUS/Sutton.html|title = Chris Sutton's home page|access-date = 2007-01-12|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130419101516/http://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/Documents/PUS/Sutton.html|archive-date = 2013-04-19|url-status = dead}}</ref>

She was Physical Sciences Editor for ''[[New Scientist]]'' magazine in the early 1980s, and has authored several non-fiction science books, most recently (with [[Frank Close]] and [[Michael Marten (writer)|Michael Marten]]) ''The Particle Odyssey'' (1987, 2002).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28744 | title=Bookshelf | website=CERN Courier | date=Nov 1, 2002 | accessdate=June 22, 2016 | author=Martin Redfern, BBC Radio Science Unit}}</ref>

She has been awarded the 2001 [[Outreach Prize of EPS|Outreach Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]], jointly with Erik Johansson, "for their innovative use of electronic and printed media to bring HEP to wider public, including professional colleagues, students and school, and in particular their collaboration developing computer interactive packages for educational master classes".<ref>{{Cite web |last=High Energy and Particle Physics Division of EPS |title=The Outreach Prizes |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/other-prize-awards.php |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch}}</ref>

== Contributions to ''Encyclopædia Britannica'' ==
